dedupe_keys.name: tunis uav wifi and bluetooth 2 4 ghz rf spectrogram benchmark

description: Researchers at the Military Research Center in Tunis recorded 2.4 GHz radio signals from a DJI Phantom 4 Pro, WiFi devices and Bluetooth devices with a USRP B210 receiver. The Data in Brief article describes drone idle, take-off, hover and movement scenarios alongside periods without a drone. The Mendeley version 1 release is a public CC BY 4.0 ZIP of about 1.47 GB. Its metadata lists 6,842 short-time Fourier spectrogram PNG images and paired YOLO text annotations for drone, WiFi and Bluetooth signal classes, including indoor and semi-controlled outdoor interference conditions. Coverage is selected transmitter types and receiver arrangements in Tunisia, not a calibrated survey of all airport or urban radio environments. Spectrogram labels do not by themselves provide raw IQ waveforms, detection range or field false-alarm rates; the archive was not opened. A reviewer-assessed use is testing RF-drone detection components in airport or critical-facility security simulations. data-nist-rf-interference-industrial-machinery is a related RF interference resource, but frequency content and annotation rules were not compared. No ZIP, signal file or article PDF was downloaded.
